previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing persistent abdominal pain and increased discharge from her G-tube following an incident where she stepped on the tube. Initial evaluation raised concern for possible dislodgement or perforation, so she was kept NPO and underwent a G-tube sinogram, which confirmed the tube was correctly positioned with no evidence of leakage. She was restarted on tube feeds, which she tolerated well, and her skin erythema improved with proper wound care. Pain was managed with medication, and she remained stable throughout the admission. She was discharged home with instructions for ongoing wound care, medication management, and follow-up with surgery clinic for possible tube repositioning.
problems: Other specified procedures as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient presented to the ED with multiple episodes of 
hypoglycemia into the ___'s a/w altered mental status and 
tremors. She was admitted to the bariatric service and a G-tube 
study was preformed to assess her tube, which found it was in 
the proper location and was working properly. Her tube feeds 
were continued in house and on HD#1 she did not have any 
hypoglycemic events.  She was re-started on Flagyl 500mg Q8hrs 
for bacterial overgrowth that may be contributing to her 
hypoglycemia. There was some granulation tissue surrounding her 
G-tube which was treated with silver nitrate and bactroban while 
in house. 

___ was consulted and recommend doing a fasting hypoglycemia 
work-up in house at the request of her outpatient 
Endocrinologist Dr. ___. This was completed on HD#2 on the 
floor. Insulin, glucose, C-peptide, proinsulin and ammonium labs 
were drawn and her tube feeds were stopped. She was closely 
monitored by nursing with q1hr finger sticks. She was off tube 
feeds for 12 hours before her finger stick was 55 and the final 
set of labs were drawn and she was resuscitated. All labs are 
visable by her outpatient endocrinologists. 

She was discharged on HD3 in the morning to make her outpatient 
appointments at ___. Her vital signs were stable and her 
finger stick glucose readings were from 55-110 overnight. She 
will follow-up with Dr. ___ on ___ on the office and was 
given a prescription for flagyl and bactroban.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  History of bypass surgery with G tube in place, now with
hypoglycemia.  Assess tube placement.

TECHNIQUE:  2 supine AP views of the abdomen were obtained, before after the
administration of oral contrast material through the existing gastric tube.  

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Initial scout AP view of the abdomen demonstrates a catheter with tip
projecting over the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.  There is mild gaseous
distention of the colon which is also filled with a large amount of stool. 
After the injection of oral contrast material through the existing tube, there
is opacification of the body of the stomach and proximal loops of small bowel,
similar to that seen on the prior exam.  There is no evidence of extraluminal
contrast.

IMPRESSION:

G-tube located within the stomach with no evidence of extraluminal contrast.

HISTORY:  ___ female with refractory hypoglycemia requiring continuous
tube feeds.  Evaluate for passage of contrast.

COMPARISON:  G-tube check dated ___ and plain film of the abdomen
dated ___.

FINDINGS:

Two supine frontal views of the abdomen demonstrate contrast seen throughout
the colon and the rectum.  There is gas in nondistended loops of large and
small bowel without evidence of ileus or obstruction.  The colon contains a
large amount of stool.  The G-tube is seen projecting over the left upper
quadrant.  Suture material from prior gastric surgery is re-identified. 
Visualized osseous structures are unremarkable.  There are multiple
phleboliths in the pelvis.

IMPRESSION:

Interval passage of contrast into the colon and rectum.
